orbitSummary: Geostationary orbit, 35,786 km above the equator. One orbit per day, so it appears fixed in the sky over one longitude.
description: Everything critical is redundant, 15+ year life, kilowatt-class payload.

subsystems.name: Structure & Mechanisms
subsystems.description: A 3-5 tonne satellite at launch. A central thrust tube carries the heavy propellant tanks straight down into the rocket's adapter.

slots.name: Primary structure
slots.why: Central cylinder plus honeycomb panels: the Earth deck, north/south payload panels and east/west panels.

variants.name: Bus with central thrust tube
variants.description: Aluminium/carbon cylinder through the middle of the box.

slots.name: Launch adapter / separation ring
slots.why: Interface to the rocket; a clamp band releases the satellite in transfer orbit.

slots.name: Hold-down & release mechanisms
slots.why: Hold the wings and reflectors during launch; released one by one in orbit.

subsystems.name: Communications Payload
subsystems.description: The repeater: receives TV and data signals from the ground, filters them into channels, amplifies each one and sends it back to a whole continent.

slots.name: Reflectors + feeds
slots.why: Shape the coverage on Earth. Each offset dish focuses onto its feed horn on the Earth deck.

variants.name: C-band (west) + Ku-band (east) reflectors
variants.description: Two 2.3 m deployable dishes with feeds and supports.

slots.name: Receivers / down-converters
slots.why: Low-noise amplification of the weak uplink and conversion to the downlink frequency.

variants.name: 6 receivers (6-for-4 redundancy)
variants.description: Any 2 can fail without losing service.

slots.name: Input multiplexers
slots.why: Filters that split each band into individual channels.

slots.name: High-power amplifiers
slots.why: Give each channel its transmit power. Arranged in redundancy rings (e.g. 16-for-12) so failed tubes are switched out.

variants.name: Travelling-wave tube amplifiers (TWTA)
variants.description: Efficient at high power; each tube needs a high-voltage power supply.

parameters.label: Active channels
parameters.help: Each active channel adds about 150 W of DC power.

variants.name: Solid-state amplifiers (SSPA)
variants.description: Lighter and simpler, less efficient at high power.

parameters.label: Active channels
parameters.help: Each active channel adds about 128 W of DC power.

slots.name: Output multiplexers
slots.why: Combine the amplified channels into each antenna beam.

slots.name: Switch networks + test couplers
slots.why: Waveguide and coaxial switches route signals around failed units; test couplers let engineers measure the payload.

subsystems.name: Electrical Power (EPS)
subsystems.description: Kilowatts of power: Sun-tracking wings in sunlight, batteries during the two eclipse seasons each year (longest eclipse about 72 minutes).

slots.name: Solar wings
slots.why: Main power source; unfold accordion-style after separation.

parameters.label: Panel length
parameters.help: Longer panels give more power but must still fold onto the bus face.

parameters.label: Panel length
parameters.help: Longer panels give more power but must still fold onto the bus face.

slots.name: Solar array drive mechanisms
slots.why: Turn the wings once per day to follow the Sun.

slots.name: Li-ion batteries
slots.why: Carry the whole satellite through eclipses.

slots.name: Power control unit
slots.why: Regulates the main bus: shunts excess power in sunlight, boosts battery power in eclipse.

slots.name: Power distribution units
slots.why: Fuse, switch and distribute power to bus and payload.

slots.name: Release-actuator firing unit
slots.why: Fires the hold-down releases in sequence.

slots.name: Electric-propulsion power units
slots.why: Convert bus power to the high voltage electric thrusters need.

subsystems.name: On-board Computer (C&DH)
subsystems.description: Command and data handling with full redundancy: a hardware watchdog swaps to the backup computer automatically if the active one stops.

slots.name: Flight computer
slots.why: Attitude control, fault handling, power and thermal management.

slots.name: Command decoder / telemetry encoder
slots.why: Baseband unit between the radios and the computer.

slots.name: Remote interface units
slots.why: Drive heaters, switches, valves and read sensors.

slots.name: Data bus
slots.why: Dual-channel network between all units.

slots.name: Watchdog / automatic switchover
slots.why: Switches to the backup computer if the active one stops responding.

slots.name: Command decryption
slots.why: Only authenticated, encrypted commands are executed.

subsystems.name: Communications (TT&C)
subsystems.description: Commands, telemetry and ranging. Omni and wide-coverage antennas keep contact during transfer orbit and emergencies; on station the link often uses the payload antennas.

slots.name: Command receivers
slots.why: Uplink.

slots.name: Telemetry transmitters
slots.why: Downlink and ranging.

slots.name: Omni / wide-coverage antennas
slots.why: Contact in any attitude during transfer orbit and contingencies.

slots.name: RF switches, diplexers, filters
slots.why: Signal routing between radios and antennas.

slots.name: Uplink power-control beacon
slots.why: A steady beacon ground stations use to measure rain fade and adjust uplink power.
slots.conditionText: you have a Ku-band payload, which suffers rain fade

subsystems.name: Attitude Control (ADCS)
subsystems.description: Points the antennas at the Earth to a fraction of a degree, 24 hours a day. Thrusters unload the wheels.

slots.name: Earth sensors
slots.why: Roll/pitch reference for Earth pointing.

slots.name: Sun sensors
slots.why: Sun acquisition and safe mode.

slots.name: Gyros / inertial reference unit
slots.why: Rate measurement.

slots.name: Reaction / momentum wheels
slots.why: Pointing control; one spare.

slots.name: Star trackers
slots.why: Precise attitude without the Earth sensor; needed for electric orbit raising, when the satellite can't point at Earth.

subsystems.name: Thermal Control
subsystems.description: The amplifiers turn kilowatts into heat. The north and south faces see the least Sun, so they carry the radiators; heat pipes carry the heat to them.

slots.name: North/south radiators
slots.why: Mirror-tile panels on the payload walls.

slots.name: Embedded heat pipes
slots.why: Spread the heat from amplifiers across the radiators.

slots.name: Heaters + thermistors
slots.why: Survival and operating temperatures, controlled by the computer.

slots.name: Multi-layer insulation
slots.why: The gold blankets on every other surface.

slots.name: Deployable radiators
slots.why: Extra heat rejection for very high-power payloads.

subsystems.name: Propulsion
subsystems.description: Raises the orbit from transfer orbit to 35,786 km, keeps the satellite inside its slot (north-south and east-west), and finally boosts it to a graveyard orbit.

slots.name: Orbit raising
slots.why: How the satellite climbs from transfer orbit to geostationary altitude.

variants.name: Chemical: liquid apogee engine
variants.description: A few burns of a ~450 N engine: reaches GEO in about a week.

variants.name: Electric: Hall thrusters
variants.description: Very efficient but low thrust: reaching GEO takes months. Saves hundreds of kg of propellant.

slots.name: Propellant tanks
slots.why: Fuel in the central tube, oxidiser beside it.

parameters.label: Propellant load
parameters.help: Propellant is usually the heaviest single item: often half of the launch mass.

variants.name: Hydrazine tank only (monopropellant)
variants.description: Simpler, for electric orbit raising where chemical propellant is only for attitude control.

parameters.label: Propellant load
parameters.help: Hydrazine for attitude control and backup manoeuvres.

slots.name: Pressurant tanks + regulator
slots.why: Helium keeps the propellant tanks at constant pressure.

slots.name: Attitude & stationkeeping thrusters
slots.why: Two independent branches of small thrusters.

slots.name: Valves, filters, pressure sensors
slots.why: Isolate, protect and measure the propellant system.
